terms.definition: The law that matter is never created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
terms.function: Guarantees products weigh exactly what the reactants weighed.
terms.whereItIs: The two level scales in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the bedrock law behind all of chemistry's counting.

terms.definition: The reshuffling of atoms into new substances during a reaction.
terms.function: Explains how matter changes form without being lost.
terms.whereItIs: The reactant atoms gliding into the products in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Rearrangement is the real story behind every reaction.

terms.definition: The exact match between product mass and reactant mass.
terms.function: Follows from the same atoms being present on both sides.
terms.whereItIs: The matching tallies on both scales.
terms.whyItMatters: Equal mass is what makes reactions predictable.
